title: Requirements
body: A required state of affairs, as a specification. An HQDM `sign`. The first seam of the development journey: it turns intent into checkable obligations that a Decision must satisfy and Verification must later discharge.

title: Acceptance criterion
body: The predicate that makes 'done' checkable — authored here as an expression over a named observable (e.g. `p95(latency_ms @ checkout-load) <= 200`), not prose. The same object is meant to become the Plan's work-item gate and the release gate at Verification: compile once, run as a gate later. Stored as text today; compiles to a formula AST once the engine has a runtime guard hook.

title: Priority (MoSCoW)
body: must / should / could / won't. The set of `must` requirements is the must-mask: a Decision is only feasible if its chosen option satisfies every must.

title: Is a must
body: 1 when priority is `must`, else 0 (a computed column). A Decision rolls this up into `mustSatisfied` — how many hard obligations it discharges.

title: Decisions
body: The act of deciding — an HQDM `activity` (an individual occurrent, with temporal extent: accepted, later superseded). Its ADR text (`context`, `rationale`) is the `sign` the activity produces, and `chosen` is its result. (`agreement` is reserved for governance-level, multi-party consent — a decision in general is the activity, not an agreement.) A Decision IS a configurator: its Options are candidate worlds, their consequences are computed, and you commit exactly one.

title: Chosen option
body: The single committed Option — the 'commit one row' of the configurator. Its consequences (effort, risk, what it precludes) become constraints on everything downstream.

title: Decision status
body: proposed → accepted → superseded. ADR immutability is event sourcing: a decision is never edited, it is superseded by a new one that points back at it.

title: Musts met
body: Sum of `isMust` across the Requirements this decision resolves (a rollup of a computed column). Feasibility check: this must equal the count of must requirements in scope.

title: Options
body: A candidate course of action for a Decision — an HQDM `possible_world` (a way things could go, with computed consequences: effort/risk/reversibility). The `chosen` option is the possible world promoted to the committed `plan`. (Grounding it as `sign` under-read it as a mere proposal document; it is a possibility with consequences.)

title: Effort (points)
body: Computed DOWN from the `size` choice via `lookup(sizing, size)` over the collection's `sizing` table (S=2, M=5, L=13, XL=34). Nobody types the number — the choice indexes the table. This is the configurator inversion of a tracker's rolled-up hours: consequences come from data, not an if-tree.

title: Decision → Options
body: Each Option names the Decision it is a candidate for; this relation carries the decision's `optionCount` rollup and, once `chosen` is set, the committed selection.

title: Decision → Requirements
body: Each Requirement names the Decision that resolves it; this seam carries `satisfies` and `mustSatisfied`. It is the Requirements→Decision edge of the journey — the first typed seam of the process.
